html:
The Western Gangas were a dynasty of southern Karnataka that ruled from about 350 to 1004, first from Kolar and later from Talakad on the Kaveri River.

They were called Western Gangas to set them apart from the Eastern Gangas of Odisha. For most of their history they were a middle power. They fought the Pallavas to the east and the Kadambas to the north west, and later served as allies and in-laws of the Chalukyas and Rashtrakutas.

The Gangas were great patrons of Jainism. Their minister Chavundaraya had the huge stone statue of Bahubali carved at Shravanabelagola around 983; see the Gommateshwara statue. They also helped shape early Kannada writing. In 1004 the Chola Empire took Talakad and ended their rule.
sum: The Western Gangas were a dynasty of southern Karnataka that ruled from about 350 to 1004, first from Kolar and later from Talakad on the Kaveri River.
